newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Several central bank targets ok - Swedish FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Several central bank targets ok - Swedish FinMin.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Wednesday that it was not controversial for a central bank to have more than one economic target.

"Almost all central banks in EU (the European Union) and outside the EU have a price stability target and one secondary target to support economic policies, employment and so on," Asbrink told a news conference.
"The U.S. central bank goes further. It has an inflation and employment target of the same importance."

Daily Dagens Industri reported on Wednesday that the minority Social Democratic government and its informal cooperation partner, the Centre Party, wanted to set secondary central bank targets for unemployment and growth.
Currently, the Riksbank's only target is price stability, to keep inflation at two percent with an allowed deviation of one percentage point on either side.

"A majority within the Social Democratic and Centre working groups want to have unemployment and growth as secondary goals," said Peter Eriksson, Green party member of the working group, to the newspaper.
"It is founded on rumours that are completely misleading and false...the rumours come from ignorance about how the situation is in other countries," Asbrink said.

New targets are being discussed among parties which are also deciding if Swedish constitutional law needs to be changed in order to permit Swedish membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), Dagens Industri said.
The parties will meet again on May 21 to discuss possible constitutional changes and Asbrink said he was striving for broad political support.
